newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales brisk at $64-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales brisk at $64-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday Wednesday were active at $64.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week's top price, feedlot sources and USDA said.
About 20,700 head had sold in Kansas, which brought week-to-date sales to 43,100, including 18,500 head previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.

About 47,300 had sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, which brought week-to-date sales to 78,100, including 23,700 formulated and 900 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.
Feedlot cattle prices were pressured by sliding beef prices, sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.49 to $0.77 per cwt, with 23 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. The choice lightweight beef price was quoted down another $0.63 at $97.89.
The price on lighter-weight choice beef fell $4.09 per cwt in the past week to $98.52 on Tuesday, down from $102.61 a week earlier, USDA statistics showed.
